title: Lost Indian Civilization: The Rediscovered Cities of the Indus
description:
Long before modern maps were drawn, one of the world's earliest urban civilizations flourished along the river valleys of ancient India. Cities like Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, and Rakhigarhi featured complex planning, early proto-writing, and vast trade networks before fading from human memory.

This video explores how archaeologists rediscovered these buried settlements across India and Pakistan. From the coastal port of Lothal to unexcavated desert ruins like Ganweriwal, we examine the evidence left behind by one of humanity's original cradles of civilization.

Which forgotten ancient city do you find most intriguing? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

short.narration: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is recognized as one of Earth's six independent cradles of human civilization. Around 3300 BC, early proto-writing emerged at sites like Harappa in the Indus Valley. At Rakhigarhi in Haryana, settlements date back to 4600 BCE, making it the largest known Indus site. Mohenjo-daro in Sindh grew into one of the world's first major planned urban centers. In Gujarat, the port city of Lothal featured a massive baked-brick basin built for shipping trade. Other sites like Ganweriwal in the Cholistan Desert remain entirely unexcavated under the sand. And lost cities like Naga Puram along the Ghaghara River have yet to be discovered by modern science.
